### opencode service start Help Output

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/cli-rs/crates/cli/tests/fixtures/cli/help/service.start.txt

Displays the help text for the `opencode service start` command, including its description, usage, and global flags. Use this to review available options before starting the background server.

```text
DESCRIPTION
  Start the background server

USAGE
  opencode service start [flags]

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                                                          Show help information
  --version, -v                                                       Show version information
  --wizard                                                            Start wizard mode for a command
  --completions <bash|zsh|fish|powershell|sh|pwsh>                    Print shell completion script (choices: bash, zsh, fish, powershell, sh, pwsh)
  --log-level <all|trace|debug|info|warn|warning|error|fatal|none>    Sets the minimum log level (choices: all, trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error, fatal, none)
  --print-logs                                                        Print logs to stderr (server logs require --standalone)
```

### Rust task with confirm and fetch

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/cli-rs/docs/plugins.md

Use `Setup::tasks()` and `tasks.spawn(host, f)` to start a task. The task waits for a confirm dialog and a fetch request; on success it shows a toast, on failure an alert.

```rust
fn setup(setup: &mut Setup) -> Result<(), String> {
    let tasks = setup.tasks();
    setup.command(Command::new("x.clear").palette(), move |host, _| tasks.spawn(host, clear));
    Ok(())
}

async fn clear(cx: Cx) {
    if cx.confirm(Confirm::ask("Clear?", "Clear the list?")).await != Some(true) {
        return;
    }
    match cx.fetch(Fetch::new("DELETE", "/api/x")).await {
        Ok(_) => cx.with(|host| host.toast(Toast::new(Variant::Success, "Cleared"))),
        Err(error) => cx.alert(Alert::new("Clear failed", error)).await,
    }
}
```

### Define GUI plugin with setup and main processes

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Each process evaluates the whole `./gui-experimental` file and reads its default export. Windows run `setup`, and the desktop app's main process runs `main`. Keep each process's code inside its own setup; code that runs in the wrong process gets inert placeholders instead of working values.

```tsx
import { shell } from "electron"
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export default Plugin.define({
  setup(ctx) {
    // Window code: Solid components, ctx.layout, ctx.add(Command, …).
  },
  main(ctx) {
    // Main code: electron, Node built-ins, ctx.windows.
    ctx.windows.on("open", () => shell.beep())
  },
})
```

```javascript
// Find icon only in specific hierarchy
const icon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  path: ['Header', 'Actions', 'IconSlot']
})

// Search everywhere including nested instances
const anyIcon = instance.findInstance('Icon', {
  traverseInstances: true
})
```

--------------------------------

### Initial load and background plugin boot flow

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/specs/v2/catalog-config-plugin-lifecycle.md

Illustrates building a baseline catalog from immediate sources while background fibers activate slower plugins asynchronously.

```ts
LocationServiceMap.get(ref)
  → build location layer
    → Catalog.layer creates empty catalog state
    → PluginBoot.layer activates immediately available plugins
      → ConfigProviderPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → ModelsDevPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
      → AuthPlugin installs Catalog.transform()
    → Catalog.layer applies active transforms during boot
    → apply policy
    → materialize baseline provider/model catalog
  → PluginBoot baseline ready
    → Frontend.fetchCatalog()

PluginBoot background fiber
  → install/update plugin packages concurrently
  → activate completed plugins
    → Catalog.transform()
      → transform(updateCatalog)
        → Catalog internally rebuilds
          → Catalog.Event.Updated
            → Frontend.refetchCatalog()
```

### Create a GUI plugin main setup with pairing service and screen blocker

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Use this as the entry point for a GUI plugin's main process. It wires storage, CLI service commands, power save blocker, and the Pairing contract; the default export is the plugin setup.

```typescript
import { execFile } from "node:child_process"
import { powerSaveBlocker } from "electron"
import { Schema } from "effect"
import { builtinMainContext } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/builtin"
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/main"
import { Pairing } from "./contract"
import { createDispatch } from "./dispatch"
import {
  createPairingMainState,
  pairingMainEffectFailed,
  selectBlocker,
  transitionPairingMain,
  type PairingMainEffect,
  type ServiceRequest,
} from "./main-machine"

type Waiter = { resolve: (value: boolean | undefined) => void; reject: (error: Error) => void }

const setup: Plugin.MainSetup = (ctx) => {
  // Whether main keeps the display awake; stored before in the desktop's own settings namespace.
  const stored = builtinMainContext(ctx).storage.store("keepScreenActive", {
    schema: Schema.Boolean,
    initial: false,
    from: { state: ["opencode.settings", "keepScreenActive"] },
  })

  const cli = ctx.cli
  const log = ctx.log
  const current = { state: createPairingMainState(), waiter: 0 }
  // Each running command's abort controller, and each caller waiting on a command.
  const commands = new Map<number, AbortController>()
  const waiters = new Map<number, Waiter>()

  const dispatch = createDispatch({
    read: () => current.state,
    write: (state) => {
      current.state = state
    },
    transition: transitionPairingMain,
    run: (effect: PairingMainEffect) => run(effect),
    failed: pairingMainEffectFailed,
  })

  // The OS can drop the blocker, so whether main holds it is asked each time.
  const screenActive = () => {
    const id = selectBlocker(current.state)

    return id !== undefined && powerSaveBlocker.isStarted(id)
  }

  const run = (effect: PairingMainEffect) => {
    if (effect.type === "blocker.start")
      return dispatch({ type: "blocker.started", id: powerSaveBlocker.start("prevent-display-sleep") })

    if (effect.type === "blocker.stop") {
      if (powerSaveBlocker.isStarted(effect.id)) powerSaveBlocker.stop(effect.id)

      return
    }

    if (effect.type === "persist.screen") return stored.set(effect.enabled)

    if (effect.type === "service.abort") {
      commands.get(effect.attempt)?.abort()
      commands.delete(effect.attempt)

      return
    }

    if (effect.type === "waiter.resolve" || effect.type === "waiter.reject") {
      const waiter = waiters.get(effect.waiter)

      waiters.delete(effect.waiter)

      if (effect.type === "waiter.resolve") return waiter?.resolve(effect.value)

      return waiter?.reject(new Error(effect.message))
    }

    // Remote access is a setting of the background service, so it changes through the CLI the app runs, as with
    // `opencode pair --remote`. A hung command ends at its timeout, so the next one always runs.
    const attempt = effect.attempt
    const controller = new AbortController()

    commands.set(attempt, controller)
    execFile(
      cli.command[0] ?? "opencode",
      [...cli.command.slice(1), "service", ...effect.args],
      { signal: AbortSignal.any([ctx.signal, controller.signal]), timeout: effect.timeoutMs, windowsHide: true },
      (error, stdout, stderr) => {
        commands.delete(attempt)

        if (!error) return dispatch({ type: "service.succeeded", attempt, stdout: stdout.trim() })
        log.write("error", "pairing service command failed", { args: effect.args, error: error.message, stderr })
        dispatch({ type: "service.failed", attempt, message: error.message })
      },
    )
  }

  // Queues a command. A read stops when its caller goes away; a change goes on.
  const service = (request: ServiceRequest, signal?: AbortSignal) => {
    current.waiter += 1
    const waiter = current.waiter
    const cancel = () => dispatch({ type: "waiter.cancelled", waiter })

    return new Promise<boolean | undefined>((resolve, reject) => {
      waiters.set(waiter, { resolve, reject })
      signal?.addEventListener("abort", cancel, { once: true })
      dispatch({ type: "service.requested", waiter, request })

      if (signal?.aborted) cancel()
    }).finally(() => signal?.removeEventListener("abort", cancel))
  }

  if (stored.value) dispatch({ type: "screen.set", enabled: true, started: false })
  ctx.onCleanup(() => dispatch({ type: "disposed" }))

  ctx.provide(Pairing, {
    remote: async (_, caller) => (await service({ kind: "get-remote" }, caller.signal)) === true,
    // Changing the setting stops the service, and starting it again brings it back. A window that closes meanwhile
    // does not cancel the change.
    setRemote: async (enabled) => {
      await service({ kind: "set-remote", enabled })
    },
    screenActive,
    setScreenActive: (enabled) => dispatch({ type: "screen.set", enabled, started: screenActive() }),
  })
}

export default setup
```

### Playground example session

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/process-daemon/README.md

Demonstrates a sequence of playground commands: demo, new, run a printf command, new /bin/sh, list, use 1, screen, replay 1 0, resize 72 20, kill 2, quit.

```text
demo
new
run printf '\033[32mgreen from the shell\033[0m\n'
new /bin/sh
list
use 1
screen
replay 1 0
resize 72 20
kill 2
quit
```

### Install OpenCode via curl, npm, Homebrew, pacman, mise, or Nix

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/README.md

Install OpenCode using the YOLO script or various package managers. Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

```bash
# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix
```

### Main setup with async cleanup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

main may be async. Return or resolve to a cleanup function, or register it with ctx.onCleanup(fn).

```ts
async main(ctx) {
  const socket = await connect(ctx.options)

  ctx.onCleanup(() => socket.close())
}
```

```bash

```

### Install GUI plugin via opencode.jsonc

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Install the plugin like any other plugin by adding it to the `plugins` array in `opencode.jsonc`. There is no separate GUI install step.

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["opencode-acme-plugin"],
}
```

### Combine definition, setup, and main in src/gui.tsx

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Entry point that combines the declared definition with the window setup and main setup. Export the result as the default Plugin.define call.

```tsx
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { definition } from "./gui/definition"
import { main } from "./gui/main"
import { setup } from "./gui/window"

export default Plugin.define({ ...definition, setup, main })
```

### Install OpenCode 1 with Homebrew

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/v1/content/index.mdx

Installs OpenCode 1 via the anomalyco/tap/opencode formula. The default Homebrew formula installs OpenCode 2.

```bash
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode
```

--------------------------------

### Plugin.define({ id, setup })

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Defines a V2 plugin with an id and a setup function. The setup function receives a context with access to hooks such as ctx.tool.hook.

```APIDOC
## Plugin.define({ id, setup })

### Description
Defines a V2 plugin with an id and a setup function. The setup function receives a context with access to hooks such as ctx.tool.hook.

### Method
Plugin.define

### Parameters
- **id** (string) - Required - Unique identifier for the plugin.
- **setup** (function) - Required - Async function that receives the plugin context and registers hooks.

### Request Example
```ts title="src/index.ts"
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```
```

### Create, get, and read session context

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Use `ctx.session.create` to start a session, `get` to retrieve it, and `context` to read its messages.

```typescript
const created = await ctx.session.create({ title: "Review" })
const session = await ctx.session.get({ sessionID })
const messages = await ctx.session.context({ sessionID })
```

### Example directory tree for config discovery

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/config.mdx

OpenCode searches from the current directory to the filesystem root. For example, start OpenCode from /home/user/projects/acme/packages/web.

```text
/etc/opencode/opencode.json
~/.config/opencode/opencode.json

/home/user/projects/acme/
├── opencode.json
└── packages/
    └── web/
        ├── opencode.json
        └── src/
```

### Plugin setup with ctx.use, ctx.stores, and ctx.add

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/gui-plugins/README.md

Access another plugin's contract via ctx.use(Changes) and read a declared store's value before setup. Contribute a command using the function form so labels are re-read when the language changes.

```ts
const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  const changes = ctx.use(Changes) // Accessor<Live<Changes>>
  const prefs = ctx.stores.prefs.value // loaded before setup
  ctx.add(Command, () => ({ id: "open", title: ctx.t("open"), run: () => ctx.layout.settings(ctx.id) }))
}
```

Makes a request to the running server. Example performs a GET request to `/api/session`.

```bash
$ opencode api GET /api/session
```

### Add a custom LSP server with command and extensions

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/v1/content/lsp.mdx

Add custom LSP servers by specifying the command and file extensions.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "lsp": {
    "custom-lsp": {
      "command": ["custom-lsp-server", "--stdio"],
      "extensions": [".custom"]
    }
  }
}
```

### createLatest example with fetchSummary

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

createLatest fetches whenever source changes, aborts stale requests, and never suspends. The latest result is kept while a newer request runs.

```ts
const summary = createLatest(
  () => ctx.sessions.current()?.directory,
  (directory, signal) => fetchSummary(directory, signal),
)
const text = () => summary.latest ?? ""
```

### Run the GitHub snapshot script with GITHUB_TOKEN

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/README.md

The snapshot script uses GITHUB_TOKEN when set; CI passes the workflow's own token. Never commit a token.

```bash
GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) bun ./script/github-snapshot.ts
```

--------------------------------

### Window setup with createKeyed and cleanup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Window setup must be synchronous. Use createKeyed for asynchronous work and return a cleanup function for resources like timers.

```tsx
import { Command, createKeyed, Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Changes } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/review"

export default Plugin.define({
  i18n: { en: { changes: "Show changes" } },
  setup(ctx) {
    // Runs once per active generation of Changes; the command is withdrawn with it.
    createKeyed(ctx.use(Changes), (changes) => {
      ctx.add(Command, () => ({
        id: "changes",
        title: ctx.t("changes"),
        run: () => {
          const session = ctx.sessions.current()

          if (session) changes.open(session)
        },
      }))
    })

    const timer = setInterval(() => console.log("still here"), 60_000)

    return () => clearInterval(timer)
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Type a window setup with Plugin.Setup<typeof definition>

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Window setup in src/gui/window.tsx, typed from the plugin declarations. It provides the Notes token using the declared notes store value.

```tsx
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"
import { Notes } from "./contract"
import type { definition } from "./definition"

export const setup: Plugin.Setup<typeof definition> = (ctx) => {
  ctx.provide(Notes, { count: () => ctx.stores.notes.value.count })
}
```

### Read VCS repository info, branches, status, and diff with ctx.vcs

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Use ctx.vcs to read repository information, working-copy status, or file diffs. The example shows getting info, listing branches with a search filter and limit, getting status, and getting a working diff with context.

```typescript
const info = await ctx.vcs.get()
const branches = await ctx.vcs.branch.list({ search: "feature", limit: 10 })
const changes = await ctx.vcs.status()
const diff = await ctx.vcs.diff({ mode: "working", context: 3 })
```

### Start, inspect, or cancel a command-based connection

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Command-based connections expose the same start, status, and cancel flow via ctx.integration.command. The example uses integrationID "acme" and methodID "cli".

```ts
const attempt = await ctx.integration.command.connect({ integrationID: "acme", methodID: "cli" })
const status = await ctx.integration.command.status({ integrationID: "acme", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
await ctx.integration.command.cancel({ integrationID: "acme", attemptID: attempt.data.attemptID })
```

### Create an OpenCode host and prompt a session

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/sdk/index.mdx

Use `await using` to automatically release the host's resources. Create a session with a directory location, then send a prompt.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/sdk"

await using opencode = await OpenCode.create()
const session = await opencode.sessions.create({
  location: { directory: "/workspace" },
})

await opencode.sessions.prompt({
  sessionID: session.id,
  text: "Review the current changes",
})
```

### TextNode Range Methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/plugins/figma/skills/figma-use-figjam/references/edit-text.md

SDK methods on TextNode for getting and setting properties across a specific character range (start to end indices).

```APIDOC
## TextNode Range Methods

### Description
Methods available on `TextNode` instances to apply mixed styling, fonts, fills, hyperlinks, and list options to specific character ranges.

### Methods
- `textNode.setRangeFontName(start, end, fontName)`
- `textNode.setRangeFontSize(start, end, size)`
- `textNode.setRangeFills(start, end, fills)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextDecoration(start, end, decoration)`
- `textNode.setRangeTextCase(start, end, textCase)`
- `textNode.setRangeLetterSpacing(start, end, spacing)`
- `textNode.setRangeLineHeight(start, end, lineHeight)`
- `textNode.setRangeHyperlink(start, end, hyperlink)`
- `textNode.setRangeListOptions(start, end, listOptions)`
- `textNode.setRangeIndentation(start, end, indentation)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontName(start, end)`
- `textNode.getRangeFontSize(start, end)`

### Usage Examples
```javascript
// Make "Hello" bold (characters 0-5)
textNode.setRangeFontName(0, 5, { family: 'Inter', style: 'Bold' });

// Make "World" red (characters 6-11)
textNode.setRangeFills(6, 11, [{ type: 'SOLID', color: { r: 1, g: 0, b: 0 } }]);

// Change size of "World"
textNode.setRangeFontSize(6, 11, 24);

// Get properties for a range
const fontAtStart = textNode.getRangeFontName(0, 1);
const sizeAtEnd = textNode.getRangeFontSize(10, 11);
```
```

### Run startup benchmark with strobe bench

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/desktop/README.md

Times a launch with strobe from process spawn to what a person waits for. Use the packaged builds, installed channels, install, or dev targets as shown; each launch runs in a private home and never touches the developer's app, profile, or live service.

```bash
# A returning user's launches of two packaged builds (pack each with OPENCODE_CHANNEL=beta or prod), or two installed
# channels.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target desktop --base exe:<old>/OpenCode.exe --head exe:<new>/OpenCode.exe
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target desktop --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta

# The first launch after an install.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target install --base app:opencode --head app:opencode-beta

# The dev loop's cold start, dev against this checkout.
strobe bench perf/startup.bench.ts --target dev --base origin/dev --head .
```

## desktop.launch

### Description
Opens a path with an app, or with the default app.

desktop.launch(path: string, app?: string): Promise<void>

### Parameters
- **path** (string) - Required - The path to open.
- **app** (string) - Optional - The app to use. If omitted, the default app is used.

### Use a glob pattern for bash permissions in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/v1/content/agents.mdx

Use a glob pattern like `git *` in `agent.build.permission.bash` to match multiple bash commands. This example asks for approval for any command starting with `git`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "agent": {
    "build": {
      "permission": {
        "bash": {
          "git *": "ask"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Return a cleanup function from TUI plugin setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/cli.mdx

Return a cleanup function to release resources owned by the plugin. The example subscribes to `session.execution.succeeded` and unsubscribes when cleanup runs.

```ts
setup(context) {
  const stop = context.data.on("session.execution.succeeded", () => {})
  return () => stop()
}
```

### Support V1 and V2 from same package entrypoint with server() and setup()

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

A plugin can support V1 and V2 from the same package entrypoint by exporting an object with a V1 server() function and a V2 setup() function. Spread Plugin.define(...) into the exported object so it type-checks the V2 definition separately from server().

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

### Declare a GUI plugin with Plugin.define and a global store

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Declare the plugin in src/gui/definition.ts so each setup can be typed from the declarations. The example registers a global store named notes with a count field defaulting to 0.

```ts
import { Schema } from "effect"
import { Plugin, Store } from "@opencode/plugin/gui"

export const definition = Plugin.define({
  stores: { notes: Store.global(Schema.Struct({ count: Schema.Number }), { count: 0 }) },
})
```

### Go API entitlement error response

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/console/go.mdx

Requests without a valid key return HTTP 401. Keys Go doesn't cover return HTTP 403 with a message that explains why, for example when the workspace has no active Go subscription.

```json
{ "type": "error", "error": { "type": "EntitlementError", "message": "OpenCode Go subscription required." } }
```

--------------------------------

### Use ctx.use(Browser) to access Live state and enable a command

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Use ctx.use(token) to get an accessor for a reactive Live<T> state. The example shows a command that is enabled only when the provider is active and a session exists, and calls live.value.open when run.

```ts
import { Browser } from "@opencode/plugin/gui/browser"

const browser = ctx.use(Browser)

ctx.add(Command, () => {
  const live = browser()
  const session = ctx.sessions.current()

  return {
    id: "preview",
    title: ctx.t("command.preview"),
    enabled: live.status === "active" && !!session,
    run: () => {
      if (live.status === "active" && session) live.value.open(session, "http://localhost:3000")
    },
  }
})
```

### Configure LM Studio and vLLM base URLs in opencode.jsonc

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/providers.mdx

Use when pointing OpenCode at LM Studio or vLLM on a remote host. Defaults are http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 and http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1. vLLM discovery cannot infer tool support, so discovered models start with tools disabled.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "providers": {
    "lmstudio": {
      "settings": { "baseURL": "http://gpu-host:1234/v1" },
    },
    "vllm": {
      "settings": { "baseURL": "http://gpu-host:8000/v1" },
    },
  },
}
```

--------------------------------

### SetupContext and Context interface reference

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

TypeScript interfaces defining the host APIs available on ctx, including stores, icons, and the full Context surface. Use as a reference for the properties and methods plugins can access.

```ts
interface SetupContext<D> extends Context {
  stores: Record<string, Persisted<unknown> | ((session: SessionRef) => Persisted<unknown>)>
  icons: Record<string, PluginIconName>
}

interface Context {
  id: string
  options: PluginOptions
  client: OpenCodeClient
  app: App
  signal: AbortSignal
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: () => T | undefined): Cleanup
  add<T>(registry: Registry<T>, item: T): Cleanup
  list<T>(registry: Registry<T>): T[]
  provide<T>(token: Contract<T>, impl: T): Cleanup
  use<T>(token: Contract<T>): () => Live<T>
  use<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): () => Live<IpcClient<S>>
  main<S extends IpcSpec>(token: Ipc<S>): IpcClient<S>
  t(key: string, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  plural(key: string, count: number, params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): string
  layout: Layout
  sessions: Sessions
  screen: Screen
  servers: Servers
  storage: Storage
  dialogs: Dialogs
  toast: Toasts
  attention: Attention
  tabs: Tabs
  keybinds: Keybinds
  commands: Commands
  links: Links
  embeds: Embeds
  ui: Ui
  system: System
  desktop: Desktop | undefined
  locale: Locale
  appearance: Appearance
  router: Router
  workspaces: Workspaces
}
```

--------------------------------

### Configure Atomic Chat local provider in opencode.json

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/v1/content/providers.mdx

Use this to connect opencode to a local Atomic Chat server via its OpenAI-compatible API. The baseURL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1; change host and port to match your setup. Model IDs must match those returned by GET /v1/models.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "atomic-chat": {
      "npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible",
      "name": "Atomic Chat (local)",
      "options": {
        "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:1337/v1"
      },
      "models": {
        "<your-model-id>": {
          "name": "<your-model-name>"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### runtime.catalog()

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/codemode/README.md

Returns structured descriptors for every visible tool, including exact path, description, and generated TypeScript signature. Hosts use these descriptors to render model-facing instructions.

```APIDOC
## runtime.catalog()

### Description
Returns structured descriptors — exact path, description, and generated TypeScript signature — for every visible tool. Hosts render their own model-facing instructions from these descriptors.

### Method
runtime.catalog()

### Parameters
None.

### Response
- **descriptors** (array) - Structured descriptors for every visible tool, each containing exact path, description, and generated TypeScript signature.
```

--------------------------------

### Register an integration transform to inspect and manage auth methods

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/server.mdx

Use ctx.integration.transform() to register a callback that can list, get, update, and remove integrations and their authentication methods. The example updates the "acme" integration name, updates a command method, lists methods, and removes a legacy method and integration.

```ts
await ctx.integration.transform((editor) => {
  const integrations = editor.list()
  const acme = editor.get("acme")

  editor.update("acme", (integration) => {
    integration.name = "Acme"
  })
  editor.method.update({
    integrationID: "acme",
    method: { id: "cli", type: "command", label: "Sign in with Acme CLI", command: ["acme", "login"] },
  })

  const methods = editor.method.list("acme")
  const legacy = methods.find((method) => method.type === "command" && method.id === "legacy")
  if (legacy) editor.method.remove("acme", legacy)
  editor.remove("legacy")
})
```

--------------------------------

### Support V1 and V2 from one package with Plugin.define and server()

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/migrate-v1.mdx

A package can temporarily expose both implementations from one default export. V1 calls server() and V2 calls setup(). The APIs remain separate; this shape does not translate hooks automatically. V1 object entrypoints are supported in OpenCode 1.18.29 and newer.

```ts
import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"

export default {
  ...Plugin.define({
    id: "example",
    async setup(ctx) {
      await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      })
    },
  }),
  async server() {
    return {
      "tool.execute.before": async () => {
        console.log("A tool is about to run")
      },
    }
  },
}
```

### Run cargo commands via bun run cargo

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/cli-rs/docs/testing.md

Use the package script to run cargo commands; it installs OpenTUI's native library and runs where .cargo/config.toml is. Includes formatting, linting, and test commands, with examples for running a specific TUI test area or unit tests.

```sh
bun run cargo fmt --check
bun run cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
bun run cargo test
bun run cargo test -p opencode-tui --test all tabs::      # one area of the TUI's tests
bun run cargo test -p opencode-tui --lib                  # its unit tests
```

### Run subagent-eviction.ts with DEMO_LABEL=AFTER

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/script/drive/subagent-eviction.md

Executes the subagent eviction proof script using opencode-drive to assert successful delivery after parent location eviction and rebuild. Requires Bun 1.4.2, opencode-drive 2.1.3, and an installed V2 checkout.

```sh
OPENCODE_DRIVE_DB=proof.sqlite \
OPENCODE_DRIVE_MEDIA_DIR=$PWD/.drive-output \
DEMO_LABEL=AFTER \
opencode-drive run script/drive/subagent-eviction.ts

```

### Access plugin options via ctx.options in setup

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

Read the plugin's options from ctx.options inside setup. These are the same values the server part receives.

```ts
setup(ctx) {
  const team = ctx.options.team
}
```

### Create OpenCode client and fetch sessions with Effect

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/sdk/README.md

Initializes OpenCode and retrieves a session using the Effect-native API from @opencode/sdk/effect.

```ts
import { OpenCode } from "@opencode/sdk/effect"

const opencode = yield * OpenCode.create()
const session = yield * opencode.sessions.get({ sessionID })
```

### Read session usage data from the server store

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/build/plugins/gui/index.mdx

A session's token, cost and plan figures are in its server's data, the same reactive store the app reads for the header's "28k · $0.28". Read them there rather than from opencode's database. `step()` is the assistant step whose tokens fill the context window now; `limits()` holds the OpenCode Console budgets and Go plan allowance once `data.location.usage.sync(location)` has loaded them.

```ts
import { lastAssistantWithUsage } from "@opencode/client/solid"

const data = session.server.data
const info = () => data.session.get(session.id)

const tokens = () => info()?.tokens // this session's tokens by kind
const cost = () => data.session.cost(session.id) // USD, with subagent sessions
const step = () => lastAssistantWithUsage(data.session.message.list(session.id), info()?.revert?.messageID)
const limits = () => (session.location ? data.location.usage.limits(session.location) : undefined)
```

### Start the minimal interactive interface with opencode mini

Source: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/services/site/src/docs/content/cli/index.mdx

Use `opencode mini` to start OpenCode's minimal interactive interface instead of the full-screen TUI. Run `opencode mini --help` to see its session, model, agent, prompt, and replay options.

```bash
opencode mini
```
